notes:
Summary: Mid-market/enterprise ticketing platform focused on high-concurrency drops and checkout reliability. Went dark after procurement paused by finance; earlier demo showed queueing during simulated drops.

Call highlights / AE notes:
- CTO (M. Alvarez) repeatedly: "cannot risk any checkout timeouts during drops; even short queueing = lost revenue".
- PoC (hosted) ran for 48h: baseline 500 QPS, spikes simulated to 8k QPS; observed queueing/backpressure for 30-90s during peak bursts, tail latencies > 600ms on critical checkout route.
- Desired SLO: tail P95 < 120ms for checkout tokenization + price calc path; tolerates slightly higher for recommendations.
- Preferred flow: Dedicated pool with fast warm-up/autoscale + burst credits to handle 5-10x peak for 10-30s. Concern: cost of keeping headroom vs. risk of missed sales.
- Security: needs SOC2 + EU data residency for EU events; internal SecOps requested KMS proof and audit log sample (ticket SEC-3322).
- Competitor note: ScaleLabs promised an "elastic burst" SKU with pay-per-spike; procurement liked the price modeling there. Customer verbally indicated price was deciding factor before freeze.
- Internal issues: product owner moved teams (no internal champion), procurement put vendor spends on hold (budget freeze).

Current sentiment: warm but blocked. AE has not heard back from VP of Finance since budget hold email (2/20). Team asked for a spike-tested PoC using Dedicated nodes with a pre-populated KV/prefix cache to show cold-start/warm-up behavior under realistic seat-allocation workflows.

Suggested next moves (from AE/SE):
- Provide 48h dedicated-burst PoC runbook + cost transparency sheet (include simulated 10k short bursts).
- Share anonymized benchmark logs showing queue depth and tail-latency before/after cache + batching.
- Offer time-limited price protection for committed burst credits to address finance concerns.
- Reconnect with product owner once internal reorg settles or escalate to procurement sponsor (VP of Ops).
